newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Vietnam buys 161,500/T gas oil in 4Q tender so far.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam buys 161,500/T gas oil in 4Q tender so far.

text.p: State-owned Vietnam National Petroleum Import-Export Corp (Petrolimex) has purchased 161,500 tonnes of gas oil in its tender for October-December deliveries and is seeking two more cargoes, an industry source said on Friday.
It bought one 23,000-tonne cargo of 1.0-percent sulphur gas oil from Japanese trader Sumitomo for October delivery on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Ho Chi Minh City.

For November, Petrolimex bought one 22,500-tonne cargo of 1.0-percent sulphur grade from Singapore trader Hin Leong, c-and-f Hongai, and one 23,000-tonne cargo of 0.5-percent sulphur grade from Japanese trader Mitsui, c-and-f Ho Chi Minh City.

In December, it bought one 23,000-tonne cargo of 0.5-percent sulphur gas oil from Mediterranean trader BB Energy to Ho Chi Minh City. It also bought two 22,500-tonne cargoes of 1.0-percent sulphur grade from Hin Leong to Hongai.
The cargoes for both grades were awarded around 95 cents a barrel premium to Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f Ho Chi Minh City, and around $1.10-premium c-and-f Hongai.
The source said Petrolimex is still negotiating to buy two more cargoes of 1.0-percent sulphur gas oil, to be delivered in November and December each to Hongai.

No 1.0-percent sulphur cargoes were awarded for December delivery to Ho Chi Minh City as Petrolimex will take delivery of an additional term cargo from Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC). This will mean Vietnam will take three 1.0-percent sulphur cargoes from KPC through its term contract in December.
The source said, Petrolimex has also awarded two free-on-board combination cargoes of gas oil and jet-kerosene fuel in the fourth quarter tender.

One cargo, comprising 10,000 tonnes each of gas oil and jet fuel was awarded to Shell Singapore. The price was a 20-cent premium for gas oil and a 15-cent premium for jet fuel, for October lifting fob Singapore.

Another cargo, comprising 15,000 tonnes of gas oil and 5,000 tonnes of kerosene, was awarded to Esso Singapore. The gas oil price was a 15-cent premium, and kerosene was a 10-cent premium, for November lifting, fob Singapore.
No fob cargoes were awarded for December lifting as the Petrolimex vessel would be undergoing maintenance during that period, the source added.
